newsitem.title: USA: Dakota Mining sets debenture sale.
newsitem.headline: Dakota Mining sets debenture sale.

text.p: Dakota Mining Corp said Tuesday it agreed to offer by way of private placement 25,000 Special Warrants at a price of C$1,000 each, representing gross proceeds of C$25 million.
Dakota said the financing is being undertaken in connection with the proposed merger with USMX Inc which was announced on January 6.

At the closing of the private placement, which is scheduled to occur on February 4, Dakota will be entitled to an immediate release of US $5 million of the proceeds from the sale of the Special Warrants, the company said.
The remaining proceeds will be deposited into escrow pending completion of the proposed merger and shareholder approval of the issuance of the common shares underlying the convertible debenture.
Dakota said it will use a substantial portion of the proceeds to complete construction and to startup operations this spring at USMX's Illinois Creek mine located in Alaska.

Immediately upon signing a definitive merger agreement and mutually agreeing to terms of a loan, both of which are subject to approval by USMX's senior secured lender, Dakota will lend US $5 million to USMX.

Additional funding for Illinois Creek mine will be provided from the offering proceeds upon completion of the merger which is expected in May 1997, Dakota said. It noted the merger is subject to shareholder and creditor approval, and review by regulatory authorities.
The company said its agency agreement with the underwriters -- Canaccord Capital Corp, ScotiaMcLeod Inc and Newcrest Capital Corp -- is subject to definitive documentation and regulatory approval.
Each Special Warrant will entitle the holder thereof to receive one 7.5% unsecured subordinated convertible debenture in the principal amount of C$1,000.
Each debenture will be convertible into 500 common shares for a conversion price of C$2.00 per share, Dakota said.

The debentures will have a seven year maturity and Dakota will have the option to repay the principal in cash or common shares at a price equal to 95 percent of the weighted average trading price for 20 consecutive trading days prior to the maturity or redemption date. Interest will be payable semi-annually on June 30 and December 31.

The debentures will be redeemable by Dakota after February 2001 at 100 percent of their principal amount if the weighted average trading price of the common shares is 125 percent of the conversion price for the 20 consecutive trading days ending five days preceding the date on which the notice of redemption is given, the company said.
